prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” roofing company for every homeowner in Dallas — the right contractor depends on your needs (roof type and material, budget, timing, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, etc.). I can help you find the best fit. To get started, tell me: is this a residential or commercial job? Are you filing an insurance claim? Any preferred materials (asphalt shingles, metal, tile)?

Meanwhile, here’s a practical plan and checklist so you pick a solid Dallas roofer and avoid common problems.

How to find the best roofer for your job
- Get 3 written estimates that show the same scope (tear‑off vs overlay, underlayment, ventilation, flashing, decking repairs, disposal, permits).
- Check reviews and complaints on Google, Yelp, Angi, and the Better Business Bureau. Read recent reviews and how the company responds to problems.
- Ask for local references and photos of recent jobs similar to yours. Drive by if possible.
- Verify insurance and bonding: contractor must carry general liability and workers’ compensation (or you must get a signed waiver if they do not) — request certificates naming you as additional insured if required.
- Confirm they will obtain required Dallas permits and will follow local code.
- Ask about warranties: manufacturer’s product warranty vs. the roofer’s workmanship warranty (length and whether it’s transferable).
- Get a clear contract: start/end dates, materials and brands, ventilation plan, how decking repairs will be handled and priced, payment schedule, clean‑up and disposal.
- Avoid high-pressure sales, door‑to‑door storm chasers, and demands for large upfront cash payments. Typical deposit is modest; final payment after satisfactory completion and inspection is standard.
- Check the company’s standing: how long in business locally, business address, phone number, and tax ID. Beware of companies that change names frequently.

Important questions to ask each contractor
- Will you pull the city permits and arrange inspections?
- How many layers will you remove? (Single removal preferred for condition/weight reasons.)
- What underlayment, ice & water shield, and ventilation will you install?
- What exactly is covered by the workmanship warranty? Is it in writing?
- Who will be my project supervisor and how will I contact them?
- Do you handle insurance claims and meet with adjusters? (If applicable)

Red flags
- No physical local address or only a mobile number
- Pushy “today only” discounts or storm‑chaser behavior
- Requests for full payment up front or large cash payments
- No written contract, no permit pull, or refusal to provide insurance certificates
- No local references or poor review response

Where to look for reputable contractors in Dallas
- Google Business / Yelp (sort by recent high ratings)
- Better Business Bureau (complaints and responses)
- Angi/HomeAdvisor for screened contractors
- Local Facebook groups and Nextdoor for neighborhood referrals
- Ask neighbors who had recent roof work (see completed roofs in real life)

If you want, I can:
- Suggest a short list of Dallas roofing companies (based on public reputation) if you want names to start with.
- Help compare 2–3 written estimates — if you paste them here I’ll point out differences and things to watch.
Tell me whether this is residential or commercial and any other priorities, and I’ll tailor recommendations and can suggest contractors to contact.
